events.what: Alpöge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle, crediting Claude, announce explicit Hadamard matrices for the twelve orders below 2000 with no previously known construction (668, 716, 892, 1132, 1244, 1388, 1436, 1676, 1772, 1916, 1948, 1964)
events.ai_basis: A solution to this problem has been reported by a researcher from Anthropic, crediting a team of three humans and Claude. ... We have provisionally marked the problem as being solved by AI

judgement.doubts: The bullet is a universal statement over all k; twelve explicit matrices are finitely many instances of it (F4), completing verification up to order 2000 but settling no infinite family, so they cannot set the status. The matrices are real and checkable (Nechita verified one), so this is a notable event, just not movement under §4. The event's AI role is uncertain: the only basis is Epoch AI's provisional 'solved by AI' label and a byline naming Claude, with no first-person account from the authors of what the model produced. 'assisted' is a plausible reading for the event, but it does not affect the row, because the status is open.

corrections.why: F4: the record says the announcement gives 'explicit Hadamard matrices for all twelve orders below 2000' and that 'the general conjecture (every k) remains open'. Twelve orders are finitely many instances of the universal statement 'for every positive integer k', not a restriction such as an infinite class of orders, so the scope is instances and the event is discarded. No resolution existed before the snapshot, so the status is open.

other: with the only event discarded as instances, no event carries the status, so the row's AI role is none. The Claude credit (Epoch's provisional 'solved by AI' label) is kept in ai.basis_quote as evidence about the discarded event.
other: under §4 step 6, an open status carries a null direction. Instances do not settle anything.
